title: Local Zero WebSocket contract (brain <-> ui)
description: One JSON object per WebSocket text frame, UTF-8. This file is the single source of truth for the Python brain layer and the TypeScript ui layer. Deliberately a SEPARATE contract from ipc.schema.json even where the shapes coincide: the two boundaries version independently, and the brain is free to reshape what it forwards. Every string in every message is rendered as text; the UI never renders markdown or HTML from any field. See docs/CONTRACTS.md.

protocolVersion.description: Contract major version. A receiver MUST drop any message whose v it does not implement.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, millisecond precision, always ending in Z.

nullableNumber.description: A measured value, or null when unavailable. null is rendered as a labelled gap, never as zero. See CLAUDE.md invariant 10.

sensorCapability.description: Forwarded from the system layer. The UI builds its labelled gaps from this list so it never has to guess why a value is null.

clientHelloMessage.description: ui -> brain. First frame the UI sends. The brain MUST NOT stream telemetry before receiving it, and MUST close the socket with an error if v is unsupported.

serverHelloMessage.description: brain -> ui. Sent once in reply to client.hello, before any telemetry.

system_connected.description: Whether the brain currently holds a live pipe to the system layer. When false the UI shows a disconnected state; it never shows stale numbers as if they were live.

sensors.description: Empty array is legal and means the system layer has not handshaked yet.

systemStatusMessage.description: brain -> ui. Emitted whenever the system layer connects or drops. This is what lets the UI degrade honestly instead of freezing on the last sample when the sidecar dies.

reason.description: User-safe prose explaining a disconnect, or null while connected. Never a stack trace, never a path.

telemetrySampleMessage.description: brain -> ui. In M1 the brain forwards the system layer's reading unchanged apart from the envelope. Any future divergence from ipc.schema.json must be documented in docs/CONTRACTS.md, not left implicit.

per_core_percent.description: Forwarded from the system layer. Position IS the core's identity, and a null entry means that core reported nothing for this sample because Windows had parked it. The UI renders a null entry as a labelled gap in that core's slot, never as zero and never by closing the gap up. See ipc.schema.json for the measurement behind this.

errorMessage.description: brain -> ui. User-safe prose only. Rendered as plain text.

requestId.description: Opaque identifier for one pending approval, generated by the brain. The UI echoes it back and never invents one: an id the brain did not issue identifies nothing, and is refused.

sideEffect.description: read may execute directly; write and destructive route to approval. See docs/SECURITY.md section 4.

origin.description: Assigned by the brain where the request enters, never derived from anything a model says about itself. untrusted_content means the request exists because of content that was read, fetched or retrieved. See docs/SECURITY.md section 6.

resolvedArguments.description: The arguments AFTER schema validation and path canonicalisation - what will actually run, not what was asked for. Values are scalars only: the dialog renders each one as text, and a nested structure is a rendering decision waiting to be got wrong. Every string here is displayed verbatim and is never interpreted as markup.

approvalRequestMessage.description: brain -> ui. Raised when an invocation has passed the name whitelist, the argument schema and path containment, and needs a human. The payload is built by the brain from the resolved invocation; no part of it comes from a model. The UI shows what will run, not a description of intent.

affected_paths.description: Computed by the brain, not narrated. An empty array means the operation touches no path, not that the list was unavailable.

approvalDecisionMessage.description: ui -> brain. The human's answer to one request. This is the full extent of the UI's authority over an invocation: it may approve or reject something the brain already resolved, and it may not construct, alter or re-scope one.

approvalResolvedMessage.description: brain -> ui. Closes out a request so the dialog never lingers over something already settled. auto_approved exists so that operations trust mode let through are still visible to the user, rather than absent because no dialog was ever raised.

trustStatusMessage.description: brain -> ui. The current state of trust mode, sent after server.hello and whenever it changes. Carried as its own message rather than as a field on server.hello because additionalProperties is false everywhere and adding a field to an existing payload would be a breaking change - see docs/CONTRACTS.md section 5.

enabled.description: When true, approval is bypassed for every invocation regardless of side_effect or origin. The name whitelist, the argument schema and path containment continue to apply: trust mode skips the approval gate, not the guard.

trustSetMessage.description: ui -> brain. The only way trust mode changes. Nothing else may send this: it is not a registered capability, so no invocation can reach it, and the state file it writes sits outside every capability's allowed_roots. A toggle a model could flip would not be a feature.

providerMode.description: local sends nothing off this machine; cloud additionally permits outbound to one provider. local is the state before anybody chooses anything - see docs/SECURITY.md section 11.

providerStatusMessage.description: brain -> ui. Which model layer is in use and whether a key is stored. Sent after server.hello and whenever either changes. It reports whether a key exists; the key itself is never sent to the UI, in this message or any other.

model.description: The model identifier in use for the current mode. Display only.

has_key.description: Whether a cloud key is stored in the Windows Credential Manager. Never the key, never a prefix of it, never its length.

providerSelectMessage.description: ui -> brain. Switches the network boundary. Selecting cloud with no key stored is refused with an error rather than silently leaving the boundary open. Like trust.set this is the user's own switch and not a registered capability, so no invocation can reach it.

memoryStatusMessage.description: brain -> ui. The state of long-term memory: whether a vault is configured, how much of it is indexed, and whether search is ranking by meaning or by keyword alone. Sent after the handshake and after each scan. Memory being off is an ordinary state, not an error - the panel and the approval flow do not depend on it.

enabled.description: False when no vault is configured or the configured one is not there. The rest of the fields are then zero, and the UI says memory is off rather than showing an empty vault.

vault.description: The configured vault directory, or null. Shown so the user can see which vault is in use; it is the user's own path.

embeddings_available.description: False means search is keyword-only because no embedding model answered. Reported rather than inferred: search that quietly gets worse is the failure nobody notices.

memoryReindexMessage.description: ui -> brain. Asks for a rescan of the vault. It carries nothing: the vault to scan is the configured one, and a path from the UI would be a path the UI chose. The reply is a memory.status once the scan finishes.

credentialSetMessage.description: ui -> brain. The cloud key, crossing the loopback socket once on its way into the Windows Credential Manager. This frame is never logged, never audited, and never echoed in a validation error; the brain acknowledges it with provider.status carrying has_key, not with the value. Removing a stored key is deliberately not in this contract - see docs/CONTRACTS.md section 5.

key.description: Non-empty. An empty key is a missing key wearing the shape of a present one, and it would surface later as an authentication failure with nothing pointing back to here.

turnState.description: What the brain is doing in the current conversational turn. REPORTED, never inferred by the UI from elapsed time: the UI has no timer that advances this and no default that fills it in. Before the first turn.state frame the UI shows idle with no caption, which is the state that claims the least.

turnStateMessage.description: brain -> ui. The conversational turn state, sent whenever it changes. Its own message rather than a field on server.hello for the same reason as trust.status: additionalProperties is false everywhere, so growing an existing payload is a breaking change - see docs/CONTRACTS.md section 5.

caption.description: What the brain is saying, in its own words, or null when it has nothing to say. Null is a gap and the UI renders it as one - it does not substitute a greeting, a status line, or filler for a turn that produced no speech. Rendered as text; the UI has no markdown or HTML renderer and a repository test holds that.

detail.description: A short label for what the state is about - the capability being run, the device being listened on - or null. Same rule as caption: null renders as nothing.

toolLogMessage.description: brain -> ui. One line of the tool log, appended as it happens. One message per event rather than a replayed array: a UI that reconnects has missed what it missed, and pretending otherwise by re-sending history would let it draw a log it never actually observed.

capability.description: The registered capability name, as the guard's step 1 knows it. Not a description of intent and not a name the model chose.

message.description: User-safe prose describing what ran. MAY paraphrase content the brain fetched, which makes it untrusted text by docs/SECURITY.md section 2 - it is safe to display because it is rendered as text and never reaches the planner, and it must never be treated as an instruction by anything that reads it.

status.description: running is not a terminal state; the UI must not report a turn as finished on the strength of it.
